title: tenant-aware warmstart cost forecaster and compact quantization policy layer
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: many tenants exhibit bursty request patterns where cold KV/cache misses and conservative batch sizing cause disproportionate per-token cost spikes. This change introduces a tenant-aware warmstart cost forecaster service and a compact quantization policy layer that together reduce unit economics for peaky workloads while preserving latency SLOs.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a lightweight forecasting service (forecasterd) that consumes tenant request histograms and predicts short-horizon load to proactively seed KV caches and adjust prefill/microbatch windows.
- Introduces a compact quantization policy DSL and a default policy pack that maps workload signatures to conservative quant profiles (int8/int4+gemm knobs) with safety fallbacks.
- Wires the forecaster output into serving runtime heuristics: prefill size, rolling microbatch window, and cache TTL tuning.
- Safety & observability: adds guardrails that prevent warmstart when tail latency budgets are threatened; extensive telemetry for cost delta, latency, cache hit-rate, and quantization-induced model divergence.

Changes included:
- A new service: infra/forecasterd (golang service, small in-memory sliding windows + protobuf API).
- A policy registry and compact DSL under runtime/quant/policies with default tenant mappings.
- Runtime hooks to read forecaster decisions in runtime/allocator and runtime/cache.
- End-to-end e2e integration tests and a smoke runner in infra/ci/prefill-smoke.
- Console and metrics: dashboards and new telemetry metrics (prefill.prediction_accuracy, prefill.cost_delta, quant.policy_applied, forecast.window_size).

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc (ENG-6821) linked
- [x] Unit tests for forecaster logic and DSL parser
- [x] E2E smoke tests for warmstart behavior
- [x] Telemetry and dashboard definitions
- [x] Canary rollout plan documented

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy forecasterd in staging and enable dry-run mode (decisions logged, not applied). Monitor prediction_accuracy and false positive warmstarts for 72h.
2) Canary apply for 5% tenant cohort with conservative defaults (small prefill, TTL 30s, quant fallback to fp16 if divergence > threshold). Monitor prefill.cost_delta and 99p latency.
3) Gradual ramp to 25% after 24h if metrics stable, then 100% with step-down safety triggers.

Operational notes:
- The default policy pack targets inference families (chat, completion, embeddings) and is intentionally conservative for chat workloads.
- Breaking changes: none to public API. Forecaster runs behind feature flag (runtime.feature.warmstart_forecaster).
- Risk: quant policy may increase model drift; mitigation includes sample-based quality checks and automatic rollback if eval loss crosses threshold.

Related: Linear ENG-6821, ENG-7043; discussion thread: internal link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-6821/tenant-warmstart-forecaster
commits: 3 commits: 1) add forecasterd service + proto + basic in-memory windowing; 2) quant policy DSL parser, default policy pack, and mapping table; 3) runtime integration hooks and canary feature flag + tests
review_threads: Noah Chen: Can we make the forecaster windowing configurable per-tenant? Author: Yes — added tenant.window_size with global default; we can expose later via Console.

Priya Raman: Quant policies look sensible but add an explicit automatic rollback on eval divergence. Author: Added sample-based eval checks and policy_applied metrics; rollback triggers if sample_loss delta > 2x baseline.
Luca Ferraro: CI flakes in the prefill-smoke on AMD instances. Author: Adjusted smoke runner to skip on AMD until runtime kernel parity is verified.
Noah Chen: Approving after nit fixes. (APPROVED)
release_notes: Introduce tenant warmstart forecaster and compact quantization policy pack. Adds feature-flagged warmstart decisions, conservative default policies, and observability to track cost/latency impact. Rollout controlled via canary.
